sources.title: GitHub - maxffarrell/julia-coreai: Apple Core AI conversion of ...
sources.snippet: This project converts SupersonicLabs/Julia-1 to an Apple Core AI .aimodel and provides a Python host adapter for Julia's decision APIs. The conversion uses the released Julia PyTorch implementation and Apple's coreai-torch converter. Julia is a finite-choice decision model. See attribution and provenance and license.

sources.title: Julia 1: A 144M-Parameter Decision Model Trained for $104
sources.snippet: A small AI lab in Brazil just released a model with an unusual claim. Not "beats GPT." Not "agentic superintelligence." The claim is this: a 144.3-million-parameter model that picks the right answer from a list you give it, runs on a CPU, on a tablet, on a 12-year-old laptop class of chip, and the entire training cost about R$540. That is US$104.08. The model is Julia 1, from Supersonic Labs ...
